cover.headline: A better generics business, already priced as one: complex generics lifted margins, but at ~23x Sep-28E EPS the stock sits far above its own history; our rule gives 19.5x: target {{dcf.tp|inr}}, SELL
cover.lead: Granules India makes paracetamol, metformin and a few other big molecules from the chemical up (API, granules, tablets) and sells mostly tablets (74% of FY26 revenue of ₹5,366 cr) in the US (~72%). It is moving to harder products: complex generics, led by US-made ADHD drugs, rose from 31% to 50% of finished dosages in five quarters and lifted the gross margin to a record 65-66%; Q1FY27 revenue grew 22% and profit 60%. The ₹1,762 cr promoter-led preferential issue, completed on 16-Sep-2026, leaves it with net cash. But its main plant, Gagillapur, has been under an FDA warning letter since Feb-2025, more than half of revenue is still legacy molecules it cannot reprice, and EPS was flat over FY21-FY26. We forecast EPS of ₹28.5 / 33.8 / 39.3 for FY27-29E on 27.28 cr shares, ~9% below ICICI Securities for FY28E. Five of the six brokers that disclose a method use **P/E**, and so do we: Granules' median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (17.9x), lifted 8.2% for the pharma sector's move, gives **19.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹36.6 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL**. Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹707; DCF ₹523. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Complex generics 31% → 50% of FD (FY25 → Q1FY27); gross margin 50% → 65.6% (FY22 → Q1FY27); 3rd largest US maker of controlled substances; Adderall XR share 5% → 29%. Seven of eight plants clean; net cash after Sep-2026.

arguments.h: The old problems are not gone
arguments.p: Gagillapur (~68% of FD capacity) has been under a warning letter since Feb-2025, with 9 approvals (~USD11 bn market) waiting for an FDA visit. Legacy generics are 56% of revenue and Granules held back supply in Q1FY27 rather than absorb costs. EPS ₹22.2 (FY21) → ₹24.0 (FY26).

Genome Valley (+40% FD capacity) was "very low" utilised in Q1FY27; the Senn peptide CDMO has ~USD20 mn of revenue and lost ₹44.5 cr of EBITDA in FY26; oncology starts in FY29; the green-chemistry project stalled against Chinese prices.

arguments.h: The price pays for the success case
arguments.p: ₹847 is 31.4x trailing and 25.0x our FY28E EPS against a 17.9x forward median since Apr-2021; Granules' P/E is 47% above its five-year median vs +8.2% for pharma. The DCF needs ~18% growth for 15 years. Street median target ₹959.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): gross margin once the cheaper US inventory is used up; Senn after a Q1 loss.
FDA re-inspection of Gagillapur (awaited "anytime now" on 29-Sep-2026): the outcome decides when 9 pending approvals launch.
Three controlled-substance launches over the next ~12 months (incl. Adderall IR); GLS utilisation above 50% by end-FY27.
Litigation on the two sole first-to-file products (generic Lumryz, generic Dyanavel XR).
Use of the ₹1,762 cr raised: the CMD is "very actively" looking at acquisitions.

sections.title: What Granules does: it makes the medicine from the chemical up (API → granules → tablet), mostly for the US; finished dosages are 74% of revenue

blocks.p: Granules started in 1984 making paracetamol, the chemical inside Tylenol and Crocin. It still makes paracetamol, metformin (diabetes), guaifenesin (cough), ibuprofen and methocarbamol at scale, but it now sells most of them as finished tablets rather than as bulk chemicals. It works at three steps: the **API** (the active chemical), the **PFI** (pharmaceutical formulation intermediate: ready-to-press granules, sold to other tablet makers) and the **finished dosage** (FD: tablets and capsules, sold to US retailers, wholesalers and generic companies). In FY26 FD was 74% of revenue, API 13%, PFI 10% and the new peptide CDMO (contract manufacturing for drug innovators, bought in Apr-2025) 3%. About 72-75% of revenue comes from North America, 15-16% from Europe and the rest from other markets; India is only ~4% (₹222 cr in FY26).

Inside FD there are two very different businesses. **Integrated generics** (46% of FD in Q1FY27) are high-volume tablets made from Granules' own API, such as paracetamol and metformin: cheap to make, sold on price. **Complex generics** (50% of FD in Q1FY27, up from 31% in FY25) are harder products: US-made ADHD stimulants and opioid combinations (controlled substances), extended-release and multi-particulate (MUPS) tablets, and a few oncology drugs. This second group is where the margin gains came from.

sections.title: The industry: US generics pay for reliability more than for low price; controlled substances and peptides are the few niches with real barriers

blocks.p: **US generics.** Once a drug loses its patent, many makers file copies and the price falls every year; a few large wholesalers and retail chains buy most of the volume and squeeze suppliers. What has changed since 2022 is shortages: buyers now reward makers that supply on time, every time, and are consolidating purchases with fewer, dependable vendors (GPI's President, 29-Sep-2026). That suits a vertically integrated maker such as Granules, as long as its plants stay in good standing with the FDA. A warning letter, as Granules has at Gagillapur, does not stop existing supply but blocks new approvals from that site.

**Controlled substances.** Schedule II drugs (ADHD stimulants such as amphetamine and methylphenidate; opioid combinations) are regulated by the US Drug Enforcement Administration as well as the FDA. Each maker gets a yearly quota, and both the API and the tablet must be made in the US. Quota cuts caused ADHD shortages after 2023, and wholesalers moved business to suppliers that kept shipping. The US ADHD market was ~USD10.7 bn and the controlled-substance market ~USD55 bn in CY25 (Elara, citing company data and Grand View Research). Few makers can scale these products consistently, which is why Granules calls this its moat.

**Commodity APIs.** Paracetamol, metformin and ibuprofen are made in huge volumes by Chinese and Indian plants. Prices spiked during COVID and then fell: Granules' own API revenue fell 54% from FY23 to FY25. In 2025-26 Chinese makers cut prices again (DCDA, the metformin starting material) and raw-material and freight costs rose with the West Asia conflict; Granules could not pass the increase on to long-term customers in Q1FY27. **Peptides.** GLP-1 drugs for diabetes and obesity have created a shortage of peptide manufacturing capacity; Indian CDMOs are small in this field, and Senn (~USD20 mn of revenue) is a niche player.

sections.title: Finished dosages (74% of revenue): controlled substances and complex generics drove the recovery; nine approvals are waiting on Gagillapur

blocks.p: FD revenue doubled from ₹1,944 cr in FY22 to ₹3,989 cr in FY26 (19.7% a year) and grew 22% to ₹1,093 cr in Q1FY27, even though Granules has had no new approval from Gagillapur, its main FD site, since the 2024 inspection. The growth came from the harder products. Complex generics rose from 1% of revenue in FY20 to 33% in FY26 and to 50% of FD in Q1FY27 (39% a year earlier). The engine is GPI in Virginia: Granules is now the 3rd largest US maker of controlled substances by value (8th in Jul-2025), top-3 in six of the seven ADHD products it sells, and lifted its Adderall XR share from 5% in 2024 to 29% in Aug-2026 (GPI's President). GPI moved from 74th to 27th among US generic companies in five years.

What comes next is a pipeline that depends on regulators and courts. Eighteen US approvals are pending: nine need only an FDA re-inspection of Gagillapur (market ~USD11 bn), one is from GPI and the rest wait for patents to expire. Three more controlled products (incl. Adderall IR) are to be launched over the next ~12 months. Two sole first-to-file ANDAs in the public domain: generic Lumryz (sodium oxybate ER) and generic Dyanavel XR (amphetamine ER oral suspension), combined US market >USD350 mn with potential 180-day exclusivity, timing subject to litigation; one more likely sole FTF in oncology; 4-5 further FTFs commercialising FY30-FY34. Granules files 6-10 US ANDAs a year and aims for 10-15.

sections.title: The legacy molecules: more than half of revenue still rests on paracetamol, metformin and a few others, and Granules has no pricing power in them

blocks.p: Granules' "legacy five" are paracetamol, metformin, ibuprofen, guaifenesin and methocarbamol. Legacy generics were 56% and non-legacy products 44% of FY26 revenue (AR FY26 value-creation page). The AR's BRSR life-cycle table attributes ~65% of turnover to products built on three APIs (paracetamol, metformin, guaifenesin) including their PFI and FD stages. Integrated generics (products built on own API: the legacy molecules) fell from 63% of FD revenue in FY25 to 52% in FY26 and 46% in Q1FY27. Granules does not disclose volumes or prices by molecule, so the trend has to be read from revenue and from what management says. API revenue rose from ₹975 cr in FY22 to ₹1,341 cr in FY23 and then fell to ₹619 cr in FY25 (−54%) as post-COVID prices collapsed and more API went into Granules' own tablets; PFI fell from ₹902 cr to ₹429 cr. FY26 brought a modest recovery (API +10%, PFI +25%) from new APIs and from European demand, not from price.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the legacy molecules are a real cost advantage (Granules makes the chemical, the granule and the tablet) but they are commodities. In Q1FY27 Granules held back supply rather than absorb higher costs, which tells you the customer, not Granules, sets the price. sections.title: Plants and the FDA: seven of eight sites are clean, but the biggest one has been under a warning letter since Feb-2025 and its re-inspection date is the FDA's call

blocks.p: Gagillapur, near Hyderabad, holds ~68% of Granules' finished-dosage capacity (26.8 bn dosages) and its main PFI plant. The FDA inspected it from 26-Aug to 6-Sep-2024 and issued six observations; Granules paused the site for a few days, classified OAI in Dec-2024, and received warning letter 320-25-48 dated 26-Feb-2025. Existing products have kept shipping throughout; what stopped is new approvals from the site. Granules hired three independent consultants, completed cleaning validation across the PFI, MUPS and FD blocks with dedicated equipment, closed more than 100 corrective actions, met the FDA in Jan-2026 and filed all responses in Feb-2026. On 29-Sep-2026 the ED said "we expect them to come anytime now". Australia's TGA inspected the site in Apr-2026 with no critical findings, and Brazil's ANVISA issued a GMP certificate.

**Why it matters.** Nine pending US approvals (~USD11 bn market) wait for the re-inspection, and the warning letter has cost money: ~₹60 cr of remediation consultants in FY26 and ~₹100 cr of abnormal costs in all, including failure-to-supply penalties and air freight (CFO, 29-Sep-2026), now under USD1 mn a quarter. Granules has reduced the risk by moving products to Genome Valley and GPI. Honest assessment: remediation looks thorough and the rest of the network is clean, but the FDA has taken two years to return and the timing of a re-inspection, and its outcome, are not in the company's hands.

sections.title: Growth projects: Genome Valley is built and must now fill; the peptide CDMO is small, loss-making and promises five times its revenue in five years

blocks.p: **Genome Valley (GLS)** is a 10 bn-dosage tablet plant that adds ~40% to Granules' formulation capacity. It cleared its FDA inspection in Dec-2025 (EIR, VAI) and has an EU-GMP certificate; Rx shipments have started, but utilisation was "very low" in Q1FY27 and the CFO expects it to cross 50% by end-FY27. Its cost is not disclosed separately: FY22-FY26 capex of ₹2,311 cr covered GLS, the MUPS block and the US packaging facility. Until GLS fills, it weighs on ROCE (18.0% in Q1FY27).

**Senn Chemicals (peptide CDMO).** Granules paid CHF20 mn (₹198 cr) for the equity in Apr-2025 and took on ₹150 cr of debt: an enterprise value of ~₹450 cr for a business with ~USD20 mn of revenue. FY26 revenue was ₹159 cr with an EBITDA loss of ₹44.5 cr; Q4FY26 was EBITDA positive on ₹70 cr; Q1FY27 fell back to ₹60 cr and a ₹12.4 cr loss ("project-to-product mix"). Roughly a third of revenue is development work, a third commercial supply and a third work for other CDMOs, across pharma and cosmetics, with double-digit customers. Targets: PAT positive in FY27, a ~USD50 mn run-rate with 30%+ EBITDA margin in about three years, and >USD100 mn in five. Planned spend: solid-phase reactors, purification and lyophilisation in Zurich (not quantified), then ~₹100 cr for peptide intermediates and ~₹200 cr for peptide API at Vizag. We forecast ₹250 / 313 / 391 cr for FY27-29E (~USD41 mn by FY29E), below the target.

blocks.p: Granules is not a seasonal business; its quarters move with US orders, launches and plant events. Revenue fell to ₹967 cr in Q2FY25 when the company paused Gagillapur for risk assessments after the FDA inspection, then grew every quarter for six quarters to ₹1,471 cr in Q4FY26. Q1FY27 was ₹1,477 cr, flat on Q4 (Europe −4% QoQ as Granules held back some legacy-molecule supply it could not reprice; CDMO −14% QoQ on project timing). The EBITDA margin rose from 20% to 24% over FY26 and was 23% in Q1FY27.

sections.title: Revenue stuck at ~₹4,500 cr for three years, then +20% in FY26; gross margin up 15 points since FY22, EBITDA margin up only 3; EPS ₹17-24 for five years

blocks.p: Granules grew revenue from ₹2,279 cr in FY19 to ₹3,238 cr in FY21, the COVID year, when the EBITDA margin peaked at 26%. Then growth stopped: revenue was ₹4,512 cr in FY23, ₹4,506 cr in FY24 and ₹4,482 cr in FY25. Three things hit it: API prices fell after the COVID spike (API revenue more than halved from ₹1,341 cr in FY23 to ₹619 cr in FY25), a cyber attack in May-2023 disrupted FY24 production, and the FDA's August-2024 inspection of Gagillapur, its biggest plant, led to a pause in September-2024 (Q2FY25 revenue −19%). FY26 broke out: revenue +20% to ₹5,366 cr as finished dosages grew 16% (complex generics from 31% to 43% of FD) and Senn added ₹159 cr. Over five years EPS went nowhere: ₹22.18 in FY21, ₹24.01 in FY26 (1.6% a year), and ₹21.8 on the 27.28 cr shares outstanding after the Sep-2026 warrant conversion.

The striking number is the gap between gross and EBITDA margin. Gross margin rose from 50.0% (FY22) to 65.0% (FY26) as the mix moved from API to tablets and to complex generics. EBITDA margin moved only from 19.3% to 22.1%. Where did the 12 points go? Into manpower (10.7% → 16.6% of sales: tablets need far more people than bulk API), other expenses (20.0% → 26.3%: plant overheads, freight, ~₹60 cr of FDA consultants in FY26), R&D (~3% → 5.3%) and Senn's ₹44.5 cr EBITDA loss. Some of that is temporary (remediation, Senn losses); most is the cost of running a formulation business.

The US is ~72-75% of revenue; US generic prices fall every year once competition arrives.
Working capital is heavy (29-33% of sales; inventory ₹1,673 cr); FY26 operating cash flow was 67% of EBITDA.
Governance: CMD pay ₹28.4 cr (4.8% of profit), four family executive directors, cheap promoter warrants.
The peptide CDMO is small and loss-making; the USD50 mn target is three years away and depends on customers' clinical programmes.
The stock re-rated from ~15-18x one-year-forward EPS (dates in FY22-FY24) to ~23x Sep-28E and ~25x FY28E on the 'Granules 2.0' story; it was ~19x during FY26 before the Q4/Q1 beats.

blocks.callout: **Where we disagree with the street.** Not on the direction of the business: the shift to complex generics is real and Q1FY27 was good. We disagree on the multiple. The street pays 23-28x forward earnings for a company whose own one-year-forward P/E had a median of 17.9x from Apr-2021 to Sep-2026 and that has delivered no EPS growth over five years. At 19.5x our Sep-28E EPS of ₹36.6, Granules is worth {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the street's own multiples applied to our EPS give ₹841-947, close to today's price.

sections.title: Valuation: 19.5x Sep-28E EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the price pays ~23x and the DCF says it needs ~18% growth for 15 years

blocks.p: Of the seven brokers with notes standing on 30-Sep-2026, six disclose a method in what we could read. Five use **P/E**: ICICI Securities 28x FY28E, Choice 25x FY28E, MOSL 23x twelve-month-forward, Elara 24x FY28E "core" EPS plus cash per share, and DRChoksey (18x Sep-27E in its last disclosed note). Emkay uses a sum of the parts. We therefore value Granules on **P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E)** on the post-conversion share count (27.28 cr), with EV/EBITDA and a DCF as cross-checks.

The house starting point is Granules' own one-year-forward P/E (price ÷ the next full fiscal year's EPS) from Apr-2021 to 30-Sep-2026, from tools/authoring/valuation-blend.js (every 5th weekly close, 58 points; reported EPS for FY23-FY26, our estimates for FY27E-FY28E). **Trough rule:** no year is left out. FY24 EPS (₹16.72, hit by the cyber incident) and FY25 (₹20.68, hit by the Gagillapur pause) were both above half the prior three-year peak (₹11.1 and ₹10.7). **Exceptional items** were 2-4% of profit (FY25 insurance gain, FY26 net charge), so the base uses reported EPS; EPS before them gives the same 17.9x. The median is **17.9x**. Granules is outside the nine-name pharma set, so we multiply by the set's median move, **+8.2%**, and round to the nearest half-turn: 17.9x × 1.082 = 19.4x → **19.5x**. No blend with Granules' own move, no growth uplift (sensitivities in part two). The turnaround rule does not apply: EPS never fell to a loss or near zero.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a better business than three years ago, but the price already pays for the better version; the rule says SELL

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a vertically integrated generics maker whose finished dosages (74% of revenue) are moving from commodity tablets to harder products: complex generics are 50% of FD, Granules is the 3rd largest US maker of controlled substances, and Q1FY27 grew 22% with a 23% EBITDA margin. It is net cash after the Sep-2026 warrant money. Against that: its largest plant has been under an FDA warning letter since Feb-2025, more than half of revenue is still legacy molecules sold on price, the peptide CDMO is small and loss-making, and EPS was flat for five years.

**What you are paying:** ₹847 is 31.4x trailing EPS, 25.0x our FY28E and 23.1x Sep-28E. On the street's method (P/E), Granules' own 17.9x median since Apr-2021 lifted by the pharma sector's +8.2% gives 19.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹36.6 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): a SELL under the house rule. The street's median target is ₹959; at the street's average P/E (25.5x) on our EPS the stock is worth ₹930, only +10% from here. The DCF says the price needs ~18% revenue growth a year for 15 years.

**The rule gives BUY below ~₹620** (upside to our target of at least 15%), HOLD between that and ~₹750, and SELL above it, on today's numbers. At ₹847 the stock is ~13% above the SELL line.

**Biggest swing factors:** the multiple and Gagillapur. Each 1x on the P/E is ~₹37 a share; each 1pp of FY28-29E EBITDA margin is ~₹2.0 of Sep-28E EPS (~₹39 a share at 19.5x). Without the sector factor the value is ~₹660.

**We would revisit** after a clean FDA re-inspection with launches under way, or if FY27-28 show the margin rising above 24% while R&D stays near 6%; either would support a case that the post-2024 valuation regime is earned.
